configurations.fair: the competent baseline; the callable is the external reviewer's own fp_corpus/critic/run_critic.py:competent, cross-checked against gates._fair
configurations.naive: the historical check. Provenance, NOT a comparison: it cannot emit a refusal verdict at all, so its score wherever the answer is a refusal is fixed before any probe runs.

ground_truth: the vendor's released fix, not a label written in this repository. See SELECTION_RULE.md for what was eligible and docs/cve-study.md for the design.

postfix_clean.ground_truth: the fix is in; FINDING is a false positive

prefix_clean.ground_truth: the vulnerability is present; NO_BUG is a false negative

expired_credential.description: the service the exploit step authenticates against answers 401 with an expired token. Injected: there is no real service here to expire a token.

helper_binary_absent.description: the helper process the exploit step starts is not installed, so starting it raises. The text comes from the operating system's loader.

interpreter_missing.description: the probe runner is pointed at an interpreter that does not exist, so no arm runs at all. The text comes from the operating system's failure to spawn.

probe_process_killed.description: the probe process exits before it reports anything, the way an out-of-memory kill or a crashed worker would leave it.

rate_limited.description: the service answers 429 before the exploit arm reaches the target. Injected, for the same reason as the credential mode.

scratch_dir_deleted.description: the rig's scratch directory is removed after the controls pass and before the exploit arm, so the arm's precondition check raises a real OSError.

stale_positive_control.description: the honest control's record is stamped outside this run's own window, so the control that is being relied on belongs to an earlier run. Produced by stamping the record, not by waiting, which is why it is marked injected.

target_package_absent.description: the pinned distribution is not on the path, so importing the target raises. This is the shape of a half-finished environment build.

controls_intact_only.note: the case that matters operationally: liveness and the honest control both pass and only the arm that would have found the bug fails.

seeded_breakage.ground_truth: pre-fix under a broken rig: the bug is present, so NO_BUG is wrong and a refusal is the only defensible answer

injected_modes_only.note: reported separately and NOT averaged into the headline: the failure text is chosen in this repository, and a confound table authored here recognising strings authored here is close to circular.

real_modes_only.note: the headline for this arm. The failure text is written by CPython or the operating system, so no wording in this repository decided the outcome.

sensitivity_fair_without_reachability.note: NOT a comparison arm. The same reviewer callable, denied only the derived record of whether the treatment arm reached the target. It answers how much of the lattice's value that one record carries, and it is never averaged into any headline.

study: known-fixed public CVEs, pre-fix and post-fix

targets.fix_evidence: 5.4's FullConstructor refuses the python/object/new tag path that 5.3.1 accepts, so the same document raises ConstructorError instead of constructing a type.
targets.notes: Acquired from the sdist's pure-Python lib3 subtree, together with its LICENSE, because PyYAML 5.x publishes no wheel for CPython 3.12 and its C extension is optional. The cached code is the released source, unmodified, and like every other pin it lives in the gitignored cache rather than in the repository.
targets.oracle: a directory the probe never creates itself exists on disk after full_load() returns, because the deserialiser called os.mkdir. A filesystem side effect, not a substring of the document the probe supplied.
targets.reachability: yaml.full_load is the documented entry point advertised as safe against arbitrary code execution; the probe calls it directly and the observable is a real directory created during the parse.

targets.fix_evidence: 3.1.3's xmlattr filter raises ValueError for a key containing whitespace; 3.1.2 interpolates the key verbatim into the attribute string.
targets.oracle: the rendered tag carries an attribute name the template author never wrote, measured by parsing the rendered tag's attribute names rather than by searching the output for the payload text.
targets.reachability: xmlattr is a shipped filter; the probe renders a template through the public Environment API and the injected attribute appears in the returned markup.

targets.fix_evidence: 3.1.4's xmlattr filter raises ValueError for keys containing '/', '>' or '='; 3.1.3 rejected only whitespace, so a key with none of it passed through.
targets.oracle: the same attribute-name parse as CVE-2024-22195, driven by a key that contains no whitespace, so the two Jinja2 targets are not one payload scored twice.
targets.reachability: the same public filter, and the 3.1.3 pin demonstrably renders the '=' key that 3.1.4 rejects, so the two pins differ on exactly this input.

targets.fix_evidence: 2.2.3 stops treating a nameless cookie's value as a further cookie string, so the header '=__Host-auth=x' no longer yields a '__Host-auth' key.
targets.oracle: parse_cookie() returns a mapping containing the key '__Host-auth'. The probe reads a parsed field, not a substring of the header it supplied.
targets.reachability: werkzeug.http.parse_cookie is the public parser Flask uses for request cookies; the probe calls it with a header value and reads the parsed mapping back.

targets.fix_evidence: 2.4.0 replaces HMACAlgorithm.prepare_key's four-string blocklist with is_pem_format/is_ssh_key, so an OpenSSH-format ed25519 public key is refused as an HMAC secret; 2.3.0's blocklist named only 'ssh-rsa'.
targets.oracle: jwt.decode() returns a verified claim set for a token signed HS256 with a public key as the secret. The observable is a successful signature verification.
targets.reachability: the probe generates a throwaway ed25519 key pair in-process, uses only its public half, and 2.3.0 both signs and verifies with it while 2.4.0 raises InvalidKeyError. No network and no pre-existing key material.

targets.fix_evidence: 2.10.1 compares the iss claim for equality; 2.10.0 used a containment test, so an iss of 'good' satisfied an expected issuer of 'http<local-path>/good.example'.
targets.oracle: jwt.decode(..., issuer=...) returns instead of raising InvalidIssuerError for a token whose iss is a strict substring of the expected issuer.
targets.reachability: issuer validation is a documented decode option; the probe mints its own HS256 token and the 2.10.0 pin accepts the wrong issuer while 2.10.1 rejects it.

targets.fix_evidence: 2.1.1 validates Content-Length against ONLY_DIGIT_RE before calling int(); 2.1.0 passed the raw value to int(), which accepts a leading '+' and underscore digit separators.
targets.oracle: the parser reports no error and a numeric content_length for a Content-Length header that is not a digit string. That front-end/back-end disagreement is what makes request smuggling possible, and it is read off the parser's own state.
targets.reachability: waitress.parser.HTTPRequestParser is fed raw request bytes directly; no socket is opened and no server is started.

targets.fix_evidence: 2.9.1 adds resolve_locale_filename, which applies os.path.basename to the locale identifier before joining it to the locale-data directory; 2.9.0 joined it raw.
targets.oracle: localedata.load() returns a sentinel value that exists only in a file the probe placed OUTSIDE the locale-data directory. The traversal is proven by the content that came back, not by the path that went in.
targets.reachability: babel.localedata.load is the loader Locale.parse uses; the probe writes one out-of-tree .dat file and the 2.9.0 pin reads it through a '../' identifier.

targets.fix_evidence: 3.2.11 replaces dictsort's Variable(arg).resolve with a restricted chain of __getitem__/getattr that does not invoke callables and forbids private names; 3.2.10 resolved through the template Variable machinery, which calls them.
targets.oracle: a sentinel method that the filter argument never marks as a call is nonetheless invoked, recorded by the sentinel object itself. A side effect in the target.
targets.reachability: dictsort is a built-in template filter taking an attribute path; the probe calls the filter directly with settings configured in-process, with no database and no request cycle.

targets.fix_evidence: 5.0.0 flips the allow_private_network default in flask_cors/core.py from True to False, so Access-Control-Allow-Private-Network is no longer sent as 'true' under a default CORS() configuration.
targets.notes: The pre-fix pin is 4.0.2, not 4.0.1: 4.0.2 is where allow_private_network first exists and defaults to True, so 4.0.2 -> 5.0.0 isolates the default flip. Using 4.0.1 would have confounded the fix with the option's introduction.
targets.oracle: the response carries Access-Control-Allow-Private-Network: true under a default CORS() setup -- a response header the application never set.
targets.reachability: the probe drives a Flask app through its own in-process test client, so no socket is bound, and reads the header off the response object.

targets.fix_evidence: 6.3.2 raises HTTPError(403, 'cannot redirect path with two initial slashes') in StaticFileHandler.validate_absolute_path before the trailing-slash redirect; 6.3.1 issued the redirect.

The fix's own comment scopes the vulnerable branch to Python older than 3.11; this study ran on CPython 3.12.5, where ntpath.isabs already rejects the payload and both pins return None for every variant tried. Reachability would need an interpreter this environment does not have, so the target is excluded from every headline rather than guessed at.

targets.reachability: NOT ESTABLISHED. With the stock FileSystemStorage on this platform both pins raise SuspiciousFileOperation for every traversal payload tried, because an earlier validation catches it first. The fix guards a name returned by a custom _save override, so reaching it would mean shipping a deliberately broken storage backend and measuring that instead of Django. Excluded from the headline.
